# From ore to metal
[textlink="Back to Mining & Industry" link="CMUGuideIndustry"]
## The smith's loop - [bold]Prepare:[/bold] collect ore, fuel and a suitable mold. A hammer or grinder breaks raw materials into powders where a recipe needs them. - [bold]Melt:[/bold] fuel and ignite the furnace; heat the crucible and its metal. - [bold]Cast:[/bold] handle hot work with tongs and pour into the right mold. Let the casting cool before taking it. - [bold]Forge:[/bold] put a suitable hot workpiece on the anvil, choose its recipe and follow the required tool sequence. Reheat it if it gets too cold.
## What should I make first? [bold]Sheets + parts → pipes and machinery.[/bold] Brass gets an early workshop moving; iron and steel carry it further. Stone hammer, tongs and chisel let you start before you have metal tools.
[textlink="Find furnace, crucible and tool recipes" link="CMUGuideIndustryRecipes"]
## Upgrade the production line [bold]Ore → powder → metal → parts.[/bold] Washing, separation and machine recipes add other routes. Check each machine's recipe before feeding it: powder, ingots and sheets are different inputs.
Molds used by machines are reusable unless that recipe says otherwise. Keep an output space free and clear slag when it builds up.
